messages:
mika: Heads-up: support flagged a regression in p95/p99 for text-gen endpoints ~03:10 UTC. Customer says p99 jumps of ~700ms and timeouts for some requests. They gave traces showing long pauses before token emission.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2024.07.21-azure-gpu started at 01:05 UTC -> completed 01:22 UTC across dedicated pool. Kernel image 6.2.20, CUDA driver 530.41, nvme fw push to subset.

sre-rotation: I'm on-call and looking. First question: is this isolated to one customer or widespread?

laura: So far only two projects are reporting, both on the same shard pool (gpu-pool-3). Checking infra metrics...

jorge: Correlating logs now. I see nvme util and latency spikes on three hosts (gpu-03a/b/c) starting ~02:55 UTC. dmesg shows controller reset messages and NVMe error entries.

mika: Can you paste the dmesg snippet?

jorge: Paste below: 
```
[Aug21 02:56:12] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 4 timeout, aborting
[Aug21 02:56:12] nvme nvme0: reset controller
[Aug21 02:56:15] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1048576
[Aug21 02:56:18] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: driver invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x...
```

laura: Storage tail latency (nvme_avg_lat_ms) jumped from 0.2ms to 7-12ms. CPU and GPU utilization look normal, but model runtime threads are blocked waiting on IO.

sre-rotation: Possible sequence: driver/firmware combo after deploy interacts poorly with NVMe controller under our workload. Next: mitigate customer impact ASAP. Options: move traffic, cordon nodes, rollback drivers, or firmware rollback. Firmware rollback will be slow and vendor-involved.

mika: Immediate mitigation: route customer to fallback pool (dedicated-standby-east) and reduce their batch size to lower IO pressure. Support can do the routing change.

support-bot: Routing change request created for API key proj-678 -> dedicated-standby-east. Propagation ETA ~45s.

jorge: Also kicked off fio on one suspect host to reproduce tail latency: 
```
fio --name=nvme-tail --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=512M --ioengine=libaio --numjobs=8 --runtime=90 --time_based
```
Result: after ~25s nvme controller reset observed, tail latency >10ms.

laura: After routing change, customer traces show p99 back to baseline within two minutes. That confirms the pool is the cause.

sre-rotation: Good. For remediation plan:
1) Keep affected nodes cordoned and evict workloads.
2) Roll back CUDA driver to 525.x on two canary hosts and validate with fio + model workload.
3) If rollback fixes it, do staged rollback per hardware/firmware group; else escalate to NVMe vendor for firmware analysis.
4) Add gating tests (fio + quick model token gen) to driver/fw rollout pipeline.

jorge: I started rollback on gpu-03a/gpu-03b to 525.85 and rebooted. Commands used: 
```
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525=525.85-1
sudo reboot
```
Collecting `dmesg`, `nvme id-ctrl`, `smartctl` before and after.

mika: Can we avoid fleet-wide rollback immediately? Customer prefers not to have service disruption. We'll do targeted rollback for nodes with same NVMe controller family.

laura: After driver rollback on gpu-03a, ran fio and model smoke test. nvme tail latency returned to ~0.3ms, no controller resets in dmesg. Model requests show no stalls.

sre-rotation: Excellent. Decision: staged rollback for nodes with matching controller vendor/model + kernel combo. Tom (infra-eng) will own automation; schedule batches of 4 with smoke tests.

mika: I'm drafting the customer note: explain we've routed them to a healthy pool, investigated and found storage controller resets correlated with recent infra change, performed targeted driver rollback which restored stability on canaries, and we're rolling out staged fixes and adding guardrails. Offer credit and follow-up postmortem.

support-bot: Customer notified; they acknowledged and accepted routing for now.

laura: Action items I recorded:
- Create compatibility matrix (kernel / CUDA driver / nvme fw)  owner: infra-eng
- Add fio + token-smoke gate in image promotion pipeline  owner: eng-qa
- Staged rollback automation runbook and label nodes for rollback  owner: jorge
- Vendor escalation if rollback fails on any node  owner: infra-eng
- Postmortem & customer summary  owner: mika

sre-rotation: Incident logged INC-2024-1599. Impact: elevated tail latency for a subset of dedicated GPU pool customers for ~35 minutes until routing and canary rollback mitigated.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged. Will monitor for reoccurrence for 72h.

mika: Anything else? If not, I'll close the active incident channel and move this to postmortem doc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
